so removing it in OpenSSH is pretty easy: it's not requested by default in the client already. When the client does, it requests zlib@openssh.com,none so it falls back gracefully to no-compression if the server has disabled it.
So disabling it in OpenSSH initially looks like turning it off by default in the server.
